answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps each account’s influence and lets anyone challenge a suspicious cluster; if linked accounts violate the rules, an arbitrator can slash their deposits. A fake identity is therefore not free: multiplying identities requires tying up more capital, while a coordinated attack risks losing it. Names like saffron, vertex, and willow may differ, but each account still has to pay the same costly bond.
